evidence: ASK: instruction.md:1-13 asks for a multi-role full-stack recruiting workspace: per-job pipeline board with one-step moves via ordinary controls, shared manual order, Interview capacity, refused moves restored with a reason naming the colleague (409 stale version), all-or-nothing multi-card moves, single-level undo guarded against later changes, live updates within 15 s without disturbing open card/draft/caret, conversations with 30-message paging that keeps place, per-person unread and seen state, per-user drafts that survive reload and session expiry, and a candidate portal with candidate wording and strict data isolation. hireops_rules.md sections 1-9 (lines 9-212) give the server-enforced detail (401/403/404 roles, 409 versions, Activity log, seeding once). instruction.md:15-17 requires Node/Express/SQLite at /app/server.js with durable /app/app.db across restarts. ENVIRONMENT: environment/Dockerfile only installs express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 and creates an empty git-initialised /app containing .gitkeep; nothing of the deliverable is shipped, so the work cannot be a trivial tweak. The template's instruction/notes are CHANGE_ME placeholders, so all product scope is task-authored. The reference (solution/app: index.js 27.7 KB, board.js 22.4 KB, threads.js 12.3 KB, app.js 9.9 KB, db.js 5.1 KB) shows the build is substantial. SMALLEST SUBMISSION / STUB ANALYSIS: (a) Static page or mock or browser-only save: fails gates/render (real sign-in after a refused wrong password) and gates/constraints hro_gate_shared (UI add-candidate, reload, then the card must be found by the Observer in a new independent browser context; 'A static seed response, a no-op success message or a browser-only save does not satisfy the gate'); scoring.toml gates render/constraints = 0.0 thresholds and score.py zeroes reward and the scored suite when either gate is 0. The same global browser gate is repeated in functional/polish/visual prompts, and visual normalises to zero on gate failure. (b) Single CRUD screen with sign-in, board and server-saved add-candidate (passes both gates): every one of the 12 binary functional criteria (weights 3.5-7, total 61) demands far more - e.g. the lightest, hro_unread_seen (3.5), needs messaging, per-person unread, seen state and live updates; hro_intake_restart (4.5) needs job opening with validation, case-insensitive duplicate email refusal at the field with form retained, internal notes, a message, unread total, Activity lines and a real restart_app with no reseed. Such a stub scores functional 0 (or at best below one criterion), and scoring.toml [floors] functional = 0.05 with score.py 'floors_passed = ... scores[k] > f' sets reward 0.0, so polished visuals cannot be farmed. Any single passing criterion (min 3.5/61 = 0.057 > 0.05) already requires a substantial real feature. Reward therefore requires real build work. CONFORMING ALTERNATIVE: a real app that is drag-only would fail, but the brief explicitly requires ordinary controls (instruction.md:3; rules section 3), so that is a fair failure; route/label freedom is preserved (app_context: 'never assume the reference implementation's routes, selectors or field names'). LESSONS FILE (checked every pattern bearing on this row): lesson 4 'keep gates simple: load, reload, server-backed' - gates are exactly sign-in, add, reload, independent-context readback, with strictness kept in scored criteria; lesson 3 - difficulty lies in edge cases inside core features (stale moves, undo, capacity, paging, drafts), not in a stub-passable surface; lesson 5 - the self-check sentence is present (instruction.md:13); lesson 15 - hro_intake_restart records several items, calls restart_app and re-reads all of them, so a fake persistence layer cannot pass. No instance of a pattern that would let a stub earn reward was found. RAW EVIDENCE: raw-evidence-index.json entries (workspace.cjs, results/workspace.json, server.log, screenshots, via-solve.*) hash-verified and their matching_source_files equal the frozen solution bytes; these are scripted golden observations only. No configured judge run, no stub/weak-app run and no reward-discrimination run exist; this row's verdict rests on brief, environment, gate wording and the deterministic score.py/scoring.toml arithmetic, which does not need runtime measurement. Whether the live judge would over-pass a stub (lessons 9) is a row 39/40 runtime question, not a defect in what this task asks for.
